question: What is AI Vastrā?
answer: AI Vastrā is an AI-powered virtual try-on platform. You upload a garment photo, pick an AI model (face), background, and pose, and the platform generates photorealistic images of the model wearing your garment — useful for catalog photography, e-commerce listings, and social media.

question: Who is AI Vastrā for?
answer: It is built for clothing brands, e-commerce sellers, and individual creators who need professional product-on-model images without organizing a real photoshoot. There is also a Merchant Portal for businesses that want to embed a try-on widget on their own website or kiosk.

question: Do I need photography or design skills to use it?
answer: No. You only need a clear photo of the garment. The platform handles model selection, background, posing, and image generation for you through a guided step-by-step Studio wizard.

question: How do I contact support or request a custom integration?
answer: Use the Contact Us button inside the app (for example on the try-on page) to send your name, email, and phone number along with your enquiry. Requests are tagged by source such as 'Integrate with Website' or 'Retail Store Kiosk' so the team can route them correctly.

question: How do I create an account?
answer: Go to the Register page and sign up with your email and a password, or use Sign in with Google. If you register with email, you will receive a verification email to confirm your address before full access.

question: Can I sign in with Google?
answer: Yes. Both the Login and Register pages support Sign in with Google (OAuth). This lets you skip setting a password.

question: Why do I need to verify my email?
answer: Email verification confirms you own the address and protects your account. After registering with email, check your inbox for a verification link. If it did not arrive, you can resend it from the verify-email screen.

question: I forgot my password. How do I reset it?
answer: On the Login page, click Forgot Password, enter your email, and you will receive a password reset link. Open the link and set a new password. The link is time-limited for security.

question: I signed up with Google but want to set a password too. Can I?
answer: Accounts can have a password in addition to Google sign-in. If your account has no password yet, use the Forgot Password flow with your account email to set one, then you can log in either way.

question: Why was I logged out automatically?
answer: Sessions have a 1-hour idle timeout for security. If you are away from the app for too long, you will be signed out and need to log in again. While active, your session refreshes silently in the background.

question: How do I log out?
answer: Use the Logout option in the app menu or settings. This clears your session cookie and signs you out on this device.

question: How do I change my account settings?
answer: Open the Settings page from the app menu. There you can manage your profile and account preferences.

question: How do credits work?
answer: Credits are the currency for generating images. Each generated image (one model + one pose) costs credits, deducted from your balance the moment a job starts. You buy credits in advance and spend them as you create try-ons.

question: How much does one try-on cost?
answer: Each generated image costs a set number of credits per job. When you select multiple poses in the Studio, each pose is a separate job and is charged separately. The exact credit cost per image is shown in the app and on the Pricing page.

question: What happens to my credits if a generation fails?
answer: If a job fails terminally (after automatic retries), the credits for that job are automatically refunded to your balance in the same transaction that marks it failed. You are only charged for images that succeed.

question: How do I buy more credits?
answer: Go to the Pricing page and choose a credit plan. Prices are shown in your local currency. After purchase, credits are added to your balance and you can start generating immediately.

question: What currency are prices shown in?
answer: The Pricing page displays plan prices in your local currency based on your country, with conversion applied automatically. Indian pricing is the base.

question: Where can I see my credit balance?
answer: Your current credit balance is shown in the app header or dashboard area. It updates after each generation and after any top-up.

question: Why was my job rejected for insufficient credits?
answer: Jobs require enough credits before they start. If your balance is too low for the number of poses you selected, the request is declined (HTTP 402). Top up on the Pricing page and try again.

question: Do I get free credits when I sign up?
answer: New accounts may receive a starting credit allowance so you can try the platform. The exact amount can vary; check your balance after signing up, and visit Pricing to add more.

question: How do I create a try-on image?
answer: Open the Studio and follow the guided wizard: 1) choose gender and garment type, set publishing platform and aspect ratio, and upload your garment photo; 2) pick a model face; 3) pick a background; 4) pick one or more poses (and optional lower garment/shoes if the pose supports them). Then submit to generate. Results appear in a Catalogue.
question_variants: How do I make a try-on?

question: What kind of garment photo should I upload?
answer: Upload a clear, well-lit photo of the garment, ideally on a plain background. The garment is uploaded directly and securely, then used as the input the AI model 'wears'. Sharper, uncluttered images produce better results.

question: What are the model faces, backgrounds, and poses?
answer: These are curated AI assets you choose as inputs. The face is the model's identity, the background is the scene, and the pose is how the model stands. You combine one face + one background + one or more poses with your garment to generate images.
question_variants: What do I select in each step?

question: Can I generate multiple poses at once?
answer: Yes. In the pose step you can select multiple poses (up to several). Each selected pose becomes its own image and its own job, grouped together under one Catalogue. Each pose is charged separately.
question_variants: Can I pick more than one pose?

question: When do I need to add a lower garment or shoes?
answer: Lower garment and shoes are optional and only appear when the poses you selected support them (full-body poses that show legs/feet). If a pose only shows the upper body, those options are hidden.
question_variants: Do I have to pick shoes?

question: What is the publishing platform and aspect ratio selection for?
answer: You pick the platform you are creating for (e.g. Amazon, Instagram) and an aspect ratio so the output matches that channel's recommended image shape. Common ratios include 1:1, 2:3, 3:4, and 4:5, and some platforms allow a custom ratio.
question_variants: What image size do I get?

question: Can I add a custom instruction or hint for the generation?
answer: Yes, there is an optional hint field (up to 300 characters) where you can guide the result. The text is sanitized before it reaches the generation prompt, so keep it short and descriptive.
question_variants: Can I describe what I want?

question: What genders and garment types are supported?
answer: You can choose Men, Women, Boys, or Girls, then a garment type within that category (for example topwear, bottomwear, ethnic wear, western wear). The garment types shown depend on the gender you select.

question: How long does it take to generate an image?
answer: Generation runs on GPU workers and progress is shown live in the app. Time varies with load and the number of poses, but you can watch each job move through queued, processing, and completed states in real time.

question: Is my uploaded garment photo private?
answer: Uploads go directly to secure storage via a private, time-limited upload link, and your generated results are tied to your account. Only you can see your uploads and catalogues when logged in.

question: What is a Catalogue?
answer: A Catalogue is a group of images generated together from one Studio submission. If you selected multiple poses, all of those images are organized under a single Catalogue so they stay together.

question: Where do I find my generated images?
answer: Open the Catalogues page to see all your generations grouped by Catalogue, newest first. Click a Catalogue to view every image in it.
question_variants: How do I view my images?

question: How do I download my generated images?
answer: Open the Catalogue and select an image to download the full-resolution result. Each completed image has a secure, time-limited download link.
question_variants: How do I save my images?

question: Can I delete a generated image or job?
answer: Yes. You can delete a finished job (completed, failed, or cancelled). Deleting a completed job also removes its stored output. You cannot delete a job while it is still running.
question_variants: How do I remove an image?

question: Why does my catalogue show a placeholder instead of an image?
answer: A placeholder appears when a job is still processing, failed, or its output is not yet available. Once a job completes successfully, its thumbnail and full image load automatically.

question: What is the Assets page?
answer: The Assets page lists the garment images you have uploaded, deduplicated so each unique garment appears once. It shows how many times each garment has been used in generations, making it easy to reuse a garment.

question: Can I reuse a garment I already uploaded?
answer: Yes. Uploaded garments appear in the Assets page and can be reused across multiple generations without re-uploading, which is convenient for trying different models, backgrounds, or poses with the same item.

question: What is the Merchant Portal?
answer: The Merchant Portal is a separate area for businesses that want to add a virtual try-on widget to their own website or in-store kiosk. It includes signup, a dashboard, API keys, billing, and integration documentation.
question_variants: What does the merchant portal do?

question: How do I embed the try-on widget on my website?
answer: Sign up as a merchant, get your API key, then follow the Integration Guide in the merchant documentation. It provides the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript snippet to embed the AI Vastrā try-on widget on your site.
question_variants: How do I add the widget to my site?

question: How do I get an API key?
answer: Log in to the Merchant Portal and open the API Keys page to generate and manage your keys. The key authenticates your widget and API requests.
question_variants: Where do I find my API key?

question: Is the merchant login separate from my regular account?
answer: Yes. The Merchant Portal has its own signup and login flow distinct from the consumer app. Use the merchant login to access the merchant dashboard, keys, and billing.

question: Where do merchants see their try-on results and usage?
answer: The merchant dashboard shows your try-on results and activity, and the merchant pricing/billing pages handle plans and payments for widget usage.

question: My generation failed. What should I do?
answer: Failed jobs are retried automatically, and if they still fail your credits are refunded. Check that your garment image is clear and try again. If failures persist, contact support via the Contact Us form with the details.

question: The page says I need to log in but I just logged in.
answer: This usually means your session expired due to the 1-hour idle timeout, or your login cookie was cleared. Log in again. If it keeps happening, ensure cookies are enabled in your browser.

question: My upload isn't working. What can I check?
answer: Make sure the file is a supported image and not too large, and that your connection is stable since uploads go directly to secure storage. Retry the upload; if it still fails, try a different browser or contact support.

question: I was charged but didn't get my image.
answer: Credits are charged when a job starts and refunded automatically if it fails terminally. If a job is stuck, it will eventually fail and refund; if you believe credits were lost, contact support with your account email and approximate time.

question: Images look low quality or wrong. How do I improve results?
answer: Start with a clear, well-lit garment photo on a plain background. Pick a pose suited to the garment, choose an aspect ratio that fits your channel, and use the optional hint field to describe what you want. Better inputs generally yield better results.
